title: My favorite brand!
body:
I LOVE the Woobles! 

 I've been crocheting for 3 years now, and found Woobles online when I was a beginner.
 It's for anybody, honestly. Beginners get step-to-step videos, and intermediate crocheters like myself get patterns with graphs and very clear instructions, and if I can't grasp what I'm reading, I can go back to the videos. 

 The yarn is fantastic, with acrylic, your hook can just stick straight through it, but this yarn doesn't only prevent that, but the colors are beautiful! 

 I absolutely love how good customer service is, and how quickly my Sawyer kit came.
 Crocheting Sawyer took me 3 or so hours, and it was such a unique pattern. A lovely weekend activity, I would absolutely recommend Sawyer, and Woobles as a whole.

title: Not beginner friendly
body:
As a beginner crocheter, I found this snail much more difficult than I expected. I even printed out the instructions and reached out to an advanced crocheter for help, and she also had some difficulty helping me understand certain parts of the pattern. 

 In my opinion, I don’t think this pattern should be listed as beginner-friendly. It includes several techniques that go beyond basic single and double crochet stitches. I especially struggled with the V crochet, which I found to be more advanced and difficult to follow as a beginner. 

 The project was cute and I really wanted to finish it, but the complexity of the pattern made me almost give up several times. I think this would be better suited for someone with more crochet experience

title: A perfect birthday gift and very cute, fun, and simple! Perfect for beginners.
body:
I was the recipient of this little wooble dog Buster for my birthday present. I had expressed desire to do some fun hobby and this was absolutely perfect for that. 

 1. The quality of the provided kit, materials and overall product was excellent. No complaints. All of it worked flawlessly.
 2. The end result, as you can see by my pictures, may vary a little, but if you follow the guide exactly you will certainly be able to get a very similar result to the picture on the product page. It is very accurate and very simple.
 3. The tutorial I found to be perfect for beginners but only if you use the video tutorial via the website. If you were to rely on the pdf instructions only it would be hard for someone who has no crochet experience. But the videos, now those are amazing. Simple, step by step repeated instruction which is very easy to follow and well explained at every point. I have no complaints. 

 I will say you get plenty of material and I had a lot left over so feel free to go ham once you are done with the base design. As you can see in my photos, Buster has taken on his own personality and he is very ready to tell you how it is! 

 Love it, 5 stars.

title: Fun project, but I wouldn’t call it quite beginner level
body:
I really enjoyed making Bingo overall! I bought both the Bluey and Bingo kits for my 10-year-old daughter, who is almost 11, after she asked for them. She started Bluey but found herself needing my help quite a bit and ultimately wasn’t able to finish it on her own. I completely understand that she is younger than the recommended 12+ age, but as someone who occasionally crochets myself, I could tell pretty quickly that I wouldn’t really consider these beginner-level projects. 

 There are quite a few individual pieces to crochet, position and attach, and some of the assembly requires more patience and experience than I would expect from a kit marketed specifically toward beginners. I’d personally put this closer to an intermediate-level Woobles project, or at least an advanced beginner project. 

 I also wish all of the instructional videos had been created specifically for Bingo. Some of the videos are recycled from other Woobles projects. They still teach the necessary technique, but for a character with this many details, having every step demonstrated directly on Bingo would have made the experience feel more polished and easier for a true beginner to follow. 

 That said, I had a lot of fun with it! I decided to customize my Bingo rather than follow the finished design exactly. I added legs, changed the tummy and inner ears, added eyebrows and made a different tail to get her a little closer to the look I wanted. 

 One thing I really appreciated was how generous the kit was with materials. There was enough extra yarn for me to make all of those additional pieces and still have yarn left over. Aside from the woven inner ears, I was able to use skills taught in the original instructions to create my additions simply by adapting the stitch counts. I think that says a lot about how useful the techniques are once you understand them. 

 Overall, it was a fun project and I’m really happy with how my Bingo turned out. I’d definitely recommend it — I’d just go into it expecting something a little more involved than the “for beginners” label might suggest.

title: I learned so much!
body: I had a little crochet knowledge before making Pierre, but I only knew how to crochet straight rows. With Pierre, I learned how to increase/decrease stitches, make "magic loop"s to start off round pieces, and sew crochet pieces together. These were all new to me and explained in depth with the videos. It took me around 8-10 hours to finish Pierre. I think there is a mistake in the instructions where it says to place the beak in the same row as the eyes, but on the bag, the beak is clearly one row below the eyes. If I make another Pierre, I would put the beak lower. Also, as mentioned by another review, I think the eyes would look better 5 stitches apart rather than 6 (or I didn't center the beak properly!), but I'm not going to bother tearing out the eye because it's already finished. I'd also make the stitches of the mid-body smaller because I feel I made him a bit too round by using loose stitches there. Lastly, if I were to try Pierre again, I'd put more stuffing in him. For reference, I only used half the stuffing. I'll be doing Fred and Keroppi next!

title: Toast the Shiba Inu is PAW-sitively perfect!
body:
Toast was such a fun and adorable kit to make! From the moment I opened the package, I loved how everything was organized and easy to follow. The instructions and videos made learning each step simple, and even the trickier parts felt rewarding instead of frustrating. 

 The best part is seeing Toast’s personality come together. The little Shiba smirk, eyebrows, fluffy ears, and curly tail make him look so full of character. He has the perfect goofy little smile, and finishing him felt like bringing a tiny friend to life! 

 I also loved that this kit helped me learn new crochet skills, especially color changes and adding small details. It was challenging enough to feel like an accomplishment but still beginner-friendly.  

 Overall, Toast the Shiba Inu is one of my favorite Woobles kits. Whether you love Shibas, crochet, or just want a cute little buddy to make, I would absolutely recommend this kit. Toast deserves a 10/10!  🍞🐕❤️

title: Ok so easy + cute
body:
I had always seen these kits at different stores and was always curious. The idea of crocheting sounded fun but I was worried it would be too complicated to learn. I ended up picking up this little guy at Target one day on a whim (it was the bib for me). However I was lowkey worried it would be too complicated to learn and I would not have enough patience and give up.  

 The videos literally made it so easy and before I knew it I was flying through decrease stitches and fasten offs. I finished him in 3 days. Was he perfect? No, but he was complete and I knew what to change for the next one.  

 I went out and bought Lola the Polar Bear the same day.  

 In conclusion, I guess I crochet now and have 3 other kits waiting to be cracked open. All my friends want me to make one for them and it’s honestly one of the most satisfying and soothing hobbies. Def good for relaxing and unwinding instead of doomscrolling.
